title: Cell Structure (KS4 Biology)
subject: Biology
strapline: The parts of animal, plant and bacterial cells and their jobs.
facts: All animal and plant cells have: a nucleus (controls the cell, holds DNA), cytoplasm (where reactions happen), a cell membrane (controls what enters/leaves), mitochondria (respiration/energy) and ribosomes (protein synthesis).
Plant cells also have: a cell wall (made of cellulose, for support), a permanent vacuole (holds cell sap) and chloroplasts (contain chlorophyll for photosynthesis).
Bacterial cells are prokaryotic: they have no nucleus — their DNA is a single loop, sometimes with small rings called plasmids.
Animal and plant cells are eukaryotic: their DNA is enclosed in a nucleus.
Bacterial cells are much smaller than plant and animal cells.
Specialised cells have adaptations for their function (e.g. sperm cells have a tail; root hair cells have a large surface area).
A light microscope magnifies; magnification = image size ÷ real size.

quick_quiz.q: Which organelle controls the cell and contains DNA?
Name two structures found in plant cells but not animal cells.
Do bacterial cells have a nucleus?

teacher_tips: Contrast eukaryotic vs prokaryotic explicitly — a common GCSE mark loss.
Link each organelle to its FUNCTION, not just its name.
Do the magnification calculation with units every time.
